faq: Do I have to give you my profit margins?
Margins make the plan much better, because they set the most you can pay per sale. If you prefer not to share exact numbers, ranges work, and we mark which figures are estimates.
Does the plan work for a small budget?
Yes. A small budget needs fewer channels and more patience, and we say so honestly. We would rather recommend one channel done well than spread a little money across four.
Will you change my live campaigns?
No. This is a planning service, and we do not edit your ads. You can set the budgets yourself from the sheet, or ask for a quote on management after delivery.
What if my results are different from the plan?
Plans are built on estimates, so the sheet includes rules for what to do when results are better or worse. Real numbers always win, and you can send us updates for a revised plan.

desc:
Ad budget planning across channels turns your monthly ad money into a clear plan: how much goes to each channel, what each campaign spends per day, and when to add or cut. Ecom Swift LLC builds that plan from your margins and goals.

## What is ad budget planning?

Ad budget planning is deciding in advance how much to spend on advertising, where to spend it and what each dollar must return before you spend it. It replaces the common habit of guessing a number, watching it vanish and hoping. A plan tells you what a lead or sale can cost before the business stops making money.

The key idea is break-even. If a product earns a certain profit after costs, you can afford to pay up to that amount to win one sale and no more. Every other number in the plan, from daily spend to channel split, follows from that one.

## How a budget plan changes your results

A budget plan protects you in two directions. It stops you from overspending on a campaign that has not proven itself, and it stops you from underspending on one that clearly works. Without rules, owners tend to panic after a bad day and cut spending, or get excited after a good day and double it. Both reactions are noisy, and platforms need steady spending to learn.

Planning also clarifies cash. Ad spend leaves your account before the sales arrive, sometimes weeks earlier for products with long buying cycles. Knowing the gap in advance means you can fund ads without starving other bills.

## What a good budget plan contains

- Your break-even cost per sale or per lead, worked out from real margins.
- A monthly total split across channels such as Meta, Google Search and Google Shopping.
- A daily amount for each campaign, so spending is predictable.
- A target cost per result, with a range that counts as healthy.
- Written rules for raising spend, holding it and cutting it.
- Seasonal weeks marked, such as sale periods and slow months.
- A reserve for testing new audiences or ads, kept separate from proven spend.
- Cautious, base and growth scenarios for the longer plan.
- A cash flow view showing when money leaves and when sales come back.
- An editable spreadsheet and a one-page summary you can show a partner.

## What we do

We begin with a short conversation about your goals and numbers: product prices, costs, current ad spend if any, and the result you hope for. If you have past campaign data, we study it to see what each channel really cost per result. If you do not, we use careful starting assumptions and mark them clearly as assumptions.

We then build the spreadsheet and summary. The Basic package covers one or two channels with a monthly split, daily amounts and break-even. Standard adds an editable sheet, target costs and the rules for changing spend. Premium extends the plan across several months by week, adds the three scenarios and the cash view, and finishes with a review call. We plan only; we do not touch your live campaigns unless you separately ask for that work.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Start from break-even, not from a round number that feels comfortable.
- Keep a small testing reserve apart from proven spend.
- Change budgets in modest steps, not sudden jumps.
- Review the plan against real results every month.
- Mark sale weeks and slow weeks in advance.

**Avoid:**
- Setting a budget so small that no campaign can gather useful data.
- Moving money between channels after one bad day.
- Counting revenue as profit when you work out what you can afford.
- Copying another business's budget, which has different margins.
- Treating the plan as fixed when real results differ.

## Who this is for

This service suits a store owner about to start ads who wants a safe spending limit. It suits a business already spending without knowing whether it pays, and one adding a second channel that needs to share an existing budget. It also suits a founder who must explain ad spend to a partner or investor.

## What to send and how to start

Please send your average order value or lead value, your approximate costs per product or service, your monthly ad money and any past ad reports. You can share margins as ranges if you prefer to keep exact figures private. We work from files or screenshots, so we do not need account access unless you want us to read live data, and then we ask only for view access as a partner or team member. We never need passwords.
